summary: Gone Coos County lookout: a 1927 log cabin, a 1942 wooden tower, removed by 2002 when the summit held a communications facility.

facts.design: Wooden live-in tower, 14 by 14 feet, on four legs
facts.status_note: Tower removed; a 2002 recovery note says the summit now has a communications facility and two buildings.

events.note: Log cupola cabin built, per the register and firelookout.com. A 1937 field report says the lookout house was built nine or ten years earlier.
Newspaper item: a new lookout station established on Bennett's Butte near the headwaters of Catching Creek
S.L. Miller field report: lookout house built 9 or 10 years earlier with a decayed foundation; suggests a 50-foot tower
Cabin replaced by a 14-by-14-foot wooden live-in tower. Credited to the association with AWS and FFE funds (1942 state report) and to the CCC (1943 newspaper).
Staffed under the Air Warning Service
Recovery note on the NGS data sheet: lookout tower removed; summit now has a communications facility and two buildings

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com say the 1942 tower was 30 feet (9.1 m). The 1942 survey station description says 35 feet (10.7 m). The brief's 10.7 m is kept because it is the only measured-style description of the structure; the register figure is noted here.

The 1942 state forestry report credits the association with paying for the lookout with AWS and FFE funds. A 1943 newspaper item credits the CCC under the state forester with completing it. The sources do not say whether these describe the same work.

The register and firelookout.com date the first log cupola cabin to 1927, and a 1937 field report agrees with that. A c.1935 entry describes a 35-foot state tower, which none of the other sources mention. It is not used in the story.
Firelookout.com gives about 10 miles SSW of Myrtle Point. The 1942 survey description on the NGS data sheet gives 12 miles SW. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Three sources, two of them compilations. Builder of the 1942 tower is disputed (association with AWS/FFE funds vs CCC). The register's 30-foot height and the 1942 survey's 35 feet conflict. No source gives current public access. The 2002 recovery note is the most recent description found. The c.1935 35-foot tower entry was left out of the story because it conflicts with the cabin history and is undated.
